title: Architecture review: KV-cache sharding follow-up (2026-03-20)
linked_artifacts: RFC-142 (internal): KV cache sharding and routing - confluence/142
body:
Meeting date: 2026-03-20
Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Miguel Torres, Samantha Lee, Ben Carter, Ravi Singh, Elena Gomez, Noah Chen

Purpose:
Follow-up to the RFC review for KV-cache sharding (RFC-142). Objective was to resolve outstanding design decisions around shard ownership, routing fallbacks, and eviction policy trade-offs before finalizing the RFC for implementation.

Summary of decisions made:
1) Shard ownership model: we agreed to adopt a hybrid ownership model (primary+replica) instead of pure consistent-hash single owner. Rationale: primary+replica reduces hot-spot risk during bursty traffic and simplifies replica warm-up when we scale up. Replica count default will be 1 (primary + 1 replica) with config-driven override per deployment class.

2) Routing policy & fallbacks: routing will prefer primary shard location for lowest latency but include an automatic fallback to a local replica or nearest compatible model variant when primary is unavailable or latency > SLO. Fallbacks ordered by: local replica -> same-region replica -> cached prefix in proxy -> model-variant routing (lower-cost variant). Each step increments a telemetry tag to track fallback frequency.

3) Eviction policy: default eviction will be LRU with a KV-size-aware penalty (items with large KV state get slightly higher eviction priority). We will also support a TTL-based eviction override for debug/test deployments. The team accepted Miguel's hybrid-LRU proposal with a configurable size-weight parameter.

4) Sequence-length-aware placement: short-context-heavy workloads should be pinned to shards optimized for low overhead (smaller KV memory footprint). We'll add a shard label (context-profile: short|medium|long) and the router will incorporate request context-length histogram to bias selection. This is a soft preference, not strict pinning.

Open issues and discussion points:
- Warm-up strategy for replicas: Ravi proposed background prefetch of recent KV prefixes from primaries during scale-up. Concern about network IO spikes. Action item below to prototype a rate-limited prefetcher.
- Cross-region consistency: Elena raised that eventual consistency window needs to be bounded for some enterprise customers. We decided to expose an SLA knob (strong-consistency mode) that disables immediate fallbacks and forces synchronous replication for critical keys; strong mode will be opt-in and gated behind Dedicated/Private tiers.
- Telemetry costs: Ben pointed out the increased cardinality from new fallback/label tags. We accepted this but asked observability team to provide a retention/rollup plan to avoid exploding metrics bills.

Implementation notes & constraints:
- Kernel/runtime implications: Sam noted that adding context-profile labels requires model-runtime metadata and may need minor changes to the compilation/kernel selection path to prefer certain quantization kernels for "short" shards. Plan to coordinate with serving-runtime infra team.
- Backward compatibility: We will keep existing API surface unchanged. Sharding and routing behavior will be configurable via deployment policy; default behavior should be conservative to avoid customer impact.

Action items (owner, ETA):
- Miguel Torres: implement prototype of hybrid-LRU eviction with size-weight parameter; run perf test against existing cache workloads. ETA: 2026-04-03.
- Ravi Singh: prototype rate-limited replica warm-up prefetcher; measure network/latency impact in staging. ETA: 2026-04-06.
- Samantha Lee: update router service to include context-profile bias scoring and fallback tagging; add unit/integration tests. ETA: 2026-04-10.
- Ben Carter: coordinate with observability to define fallback/label tagging telemetry and retention plan; provide cost estimate. ETA: 2026-04-01.
- Elena Gomez: draft policy doc for "strong-consistency mode" (requirements, SLA implications, pricing note) and sync with product. ETA: 2026-04-08.
- Aisha Patel: finalize RFC-142 text incorporating today's decisions and open items; submit RFC for final review. ETA: 2026-03-27.

Next steps/meetings:
- We will run the three prototypes (eviction, prefetcher, router changes) in parallel. Weekly sync to monitor perf/telemetry starting 2026-03-30.
- Hold a final design signoff meeting on 2026-04-15 to approve RFC changes for implementation, assuming prototypes do not introduce regressions.

References / links:
- RFC-142 (draft): confluence/142
- Related meeting notes: architecture-review-kv-cache-sharding-meeting-notes-2026-03-03.json
- Implementation PR template: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/678

Notes to reviewers:
- This is an in-review working doc. Please leave comments inline on the RFC doc and ping owners for clarifications. If you are responsible for observability or SRE consequences, review Ben's telemetry ask ASAP - we need an estimate before finalizing labels.

Observations from meeting (informal):
- Team leaned toward safer defaults that can be tuned per-customer rather than aggressive defaults that could cause cross-tenant impact.
- There is general appetite to push more routing intelligence into the control plane (policy-driven routing) rather than bake it into the fleet.

-- end of notes --
